title: Research radar
task: Follow a research topic and return differences that can change the project.
sources: Primary sources, research questions, existing knowledge and decisions.
adaptation: Refine sources and criteria, retain reopening conditions and avoid duplicate notifications.
attention: A difference opening an experiment, correcting a hypothesis or requiring a choice.

title: Reasoned bibliography
task: Update a work’s bibliography and connect contributions to open questions.
sources: Manuscript, references and accessible original publications.
adaptation: Improve search relevance while preserving disagreement and study limitations.
attention: A source changing an argument or method choice.

title: Experiment continuity
task: Resume authorized experiments, compare outcomes and prepare the next useful step.
sources: Protocols, data, logs and tools available in the project.
adaptation: Distinguish useful differences from repetition and return reusable criteria to the competence.
attention: A result changing a hypothesis, an error or the next experiment decision.

title: Software dependencies
task: Follow changes in dependencies actually used and prepare pertinent interventions.
sources: Repository, installed versions, release notes and official documentation.
adaptation: Connect notices to actual use, remove repetition and improve sources.
attention: A change requiring a product decision or intervention.

title: Product documentation
task: Reconcile selected product changes with the guides describing them.
sources: Source changes, product state, guides and project conventions.
adaptation: Learn which surfaces depend on a change and preserve concurrent work.
attention: An inaccurate guide or a proposal ready for review.

title: Issue triage
task: Group similar reports and prepare reproducible cases for pertinent problems.
sources: Issues, accessible logs, versions and team criteria.
adaptation: Improve duplicate recognition and the information needed to reproduce failures.
attention: A regression, reproducible case or priority decision.

title: Editorial preparation
task: Follow sources and prepare content in the forms selected for the project.
sources: Originals, selected revisions, editorial guide and content state.
adaptation: Preserve authorial distinctions and improve clarity, sources and adaptations.
attention: A useful draft for review or a question changing the content.

title: Content distribution
task: Prepare channel adaptations of selected content and follow their outcomes.
sources: Main resource, revision state, channel context and available feedback.
adaptation: Learn from responses and channel conditions while preserving source meaning.
attention: An adaptation to choose or a response deserving continuation.

title: Industry discussions
task: Find pertinent conversations and prepare contributions useful to their context.
sources: Current discussions, community rules and public project knowledge.
adaptation: Improve relevance and timing without repeating the same proposal.
attention: A conversation where the project can offer a concrete contribution.

title: Organizational knowledge
task: Keep knowledge and decision reasons affecting team work reachable.
sources: Authorized documents, decisions, guides and existing competences.
adaptation: Recognize duplicate or superseded knowledge and return changes to the relevant location.
attention: An operational contradiction or knowledge update to integrate.

title: Customer support
task: Prepare replies and documentation improvements from recurring questions.
sources: Authorized requests, product information and validated answers.
adaptation: Learn useful categories and cases needing a person; keep drafting distinct from sending.
attention: A prepared reply or a case requiring human expertise.

title: Operating procedures
task: Observe differences between a procedure and actual work and prepare situated corrections.
sources: Procedures, team feedback, tools and activity state.
adaptation: Remove exhausted steps and preserve correction reasons.
attention: A difference changing work quality or feasibility.

title: Data quality
task: Follow selected data sources and prepare corrections useful to their consumers.
sources: Authorized datasets, definitions, update processes and available checks.
adaptation: Distinguish new errors from known ones and improve detection criteria.
attention: A difference altering data use or a correction ready for assessment.

title: Website and public paths
task: Keep pages, links and public information connected to the current product.
sources: Site sources, accessible pages, product state and available feedback.
adaptation: Learn dependencies between changes, pages and paths without repeating unchanged checks.
attention: A broken path or information that has become inaccurate.

title: Project continuity
task: Prepare useful reentry across sessions or people while retaining purpose, reasons and valid work.
sources: Current guides, decisions, concurrent contributions and project sources.
adaptation: Condense context while preserving relations needed for continuation.
attention: A choice, real conflict or handoff enabling the next work.

title: Learning path
task: Prepare study and exercises from goals, acquired knowledge and encountered difficulties.
sources: The person’s goals, selected materials and exercise outcomes.
adaptation: Change examples and depth through observed understanding.
attention: A useful passage to practice or a difficulty changing the path.

title: Opportunity radar
task: Follow project-relevant opportunities and prepare a concretely useful next step.
sources: Project direction, real conditions, programs and original sources.
adaptation: Distinguish interest, accessibility and attention cost; retain reopening conditions.
attention: A possibility enabling concrete preparation or a choice.

title: Domain service
task: Form recurring work for a particular domain together with its competences.
sources: The person’s mandate, domain knowledge, tools and usage feedback.
adaptation: Let work form further methods and capabilities in the recipient’s context.
attention: A useful result, choice or difference changing the service.
